title: Migration scaffold: TF pinning, API probes, and rollback fenceposts
body:
Summary:
This doc is a practical scaffold for orchestrating minor and major upgrades in Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. It synthesizes a conservative Terraform module pinning policy, an API compatibility probe pattern, automated preflight probes, and a staged rollback fencepost design. The goal is to provide a repeatable, low-risk path to upgrade runtime and control plane components while preserving API compatibility for customer integrations.

Scope and intended use:
- Audience: SRE/Platform Engineers executing Private upgrades, Solutions Engineers coordinating customer cutovers, and Release Engineers preparing TF changes.
- Applies to: control-plane components, runtime servers (inference runtime), gateway/proxy adapters, and Terraform modules used to provision private attachments.
- Not in scope: customer application changes unrelated to our API surface (they should be covered by customer migration guides).

High-level goals:
- Zero-surprise rollouts for customers on Private deployments.
- Clear, scriptable preflight checks that fail fast during CI/CD.
- Fast, deterministic rollback with minimal state-loss risk.
- Minimal API surface churn: explicit negotiation and deprecation windows.

Key constraints and risks:
- Heterogeneous hardware across customers (GPU families, quantized runtimes) means runtime binaries may behave differently – plan for device-specific probes.
- TF state drift between appliance-managed and customer-managed resources can block automated rollbacks. Keep TF changes minimal and reversible where possible.
- Large customer KV/state migrations are the biggest outage risk; prefer online migration strategies.

Policy: Terraform module pinning and release hygiene
- Always pin module versions to exact tags in private-deployments (e.g., module 'runtime' { source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//private-runtime?ref=v2025-11-01" }).
- Use semantic-major gating: accept patches/bugfixes in minor version during a maintenance window, but require a documented compatibility matrix for major version bumps.
- Avoid multi-change commits: separate TF module upgrades (infrastructure) from config changes (feature flags) to make rollbacks safe.
- Add a terraform plan artifact to CI builds and attach it to the rollout ticket. Keep a copy in the release tag.

API compatibility probe pattern (novel approach)
- Implement a lightweight, idempotent endpoint: GET /internal/compat that returns: supported_versions, default_behavior_flags, and a checksum of runtime binary + proto descriptors. This allows probing clients to decide whether to route traffic.
- Probe sequence: 1) Control plane /internal/compat 2) Runtime /internal/compat 3) Proxy adapter /internal/compat 4) KV/cache schema probe (if applicable)
- Acceptable mismatch policy: if runtime supports an older minor version but control plane advertises new optional flags, allow continued operation. Only block when required field removal is detected.
- Maintain a negotiation table in the console: customer_id => last_seen_compat_checksum. Use this for targeted rollbacks if compatibility diverges.

Preflight harness (lab)
- A small lab script (runs locally in release CI) to exercise the entire upgrade path against a snapshot of customer TF state (redacted):
  - terraform init && terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan
  - terraform apply -auto-approve plan.tfplan in a sandbox namespace
  - Run compat probes: curl -sS https://sandbox.local/internal/compat | jq .
  - Run tokenized smoke: send 1k short requests across seq lengths for runtime and assert latency / error thresholds
- Probe automation should surface a short report: errors, percent failed, median latency, token-cost delta. Keep this report attached to the release.

Canary and traffic mirroring strategy (practical heuristics)
- Mirror-only phase: mirror 0.5% of production traffic to the new runtime for 24 hours. Monitor downstream metrics but do not serve live responses.
- Shadow + limited live: route up to 2% of requests to the new runtime with an immediate fallback on per-request failure. Ramp percentages at 15-minute intervals if canary SLOs hold.
- If any of these triggers fire, automatically flip to rollback fencepost (see below). Triggers: 5xx rate > 0.5% absolute increase, tail latency p95 > 2x baseline, quality regression on eval set > configured threshold.

Rollback fencepost design (unique phrasing: fencepost)
- Each rollout must write a fencepost marker to cluster metadata: rollout_id, timestamp, left_state_checksum, right_state_checksum. The marker is the single source to drive automated rollback.
- Rollback operator uses the fencepost to: 1) rewind traffic routing 2) re-apply pinned TF versions (if TF drift occurred) 3) restore config snapshots for feature flags
- Automatic rollback preconditions: if canary probes fail consecutively for 3 checks or a critical alert is fired, trigger an automated rollback plan with human-in-loop confirmation within 10 minutes.

Observability gating and metrics to watch (must be explicit)
- SLOs for canary: success_rate, p50/p95 latency, model-quality delta (if applicable).
- Telemetry: per-request model_version header, compat_checksum, trace_id passed through control plane -> runtime.
- Dashboards: canary rollouts should spin up an ephemeral dashboard with side-by-side old vs new metrics and request sampling for failed traces.

Stateful considerations & KV/cache migration notes
- Avoid destructive schema migrations during a single rollout. If schema change required, use additive migrations + dual-read/write window.
- For KV prefix changes, keep old prefix alive for at least 48 hours and run a background reconciler that logs divergence stats.
- If cache serialization format changes, include a deserialization shim in the new runtime that can read both old and new encodings for the deprecation window.

Checklist: pre-rollout (CI -> staging)
- [ ] Module pin confirmed and plan artifact attached to release ticket.
- [ ] Compatibility probes pass against staging snapshot.
- [ ] Smoke tests: tokenized requests, auth flows, streaming test.
- [ ] Backup: config snapshot + TF state backup exported.
- [ ] Communication: notify impacted customers + Solutions Eng assigned.

Checklist: rollout day (canary -> ramp)
- [ ] Start mirror-only for 24 hours. Collect metrics.
- [ ] Launch shadow canary with 0.5–2% live traffic. Watch for alerts.
- [ ] Confirm no API sniffers detected missing fields (use /internal/compat logs).
- [ ] If no regressions, start stepwise ramp (2% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%). Stop if any trigger fires.

Checklist: rollback procedure
- [ ] Trigger fencepost rollback via ops CLI: redwood-ops rollback --rollout-id <id>
- [ ] Reapply pinned TF modules from release tag: terraform init && terraform apply -var-file=rollback-vars.tfvars
- [ ] Clear ephemeral config: restart proxies with pinned config.
- [ ] Validate: run compat probes and smoke tests against restored state.

Postmortem & follow-up
- Capture a postmortem for any nontrivial rollback. Include: what probe failed, customer impact, TF state drift analysis, and remediation plan.
- Maintain a small orienting checklist for customers: how we will coordinate (who, when, and what to test).

Example TF snippet (recommended pattern):
module "runtime" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//private-runtime?ref=v2025-11-01"
  name   = "private-runtime-${var.customer_short}"
  tags   = var.tags
}
# keep a separate module bump PR when changing the ref

Operational quick commands (examples)
- Probe compat: curl -sS https://$CLUSTER/internal/compat | jq .
- Mirror traffic (gateway): kubectl annotate svc gateway traffic-mirror=new-runtime --overwrite
- Rollback (quick): redwood-ops rollback --rollout-id=2026-02-20-heatcheck --reason="canary p95 spike"

Open questions / items to decide
- Formalize acceptable compatibility delta numbers for model-quality regressions. Do we require a numeric quota?
- Decide maximum sane runtime binary size/time for the compat checksum handshake.
- Should TF auto-rollback attempt to rewrite provider state on behalf of customers, or require manual approval?

Appendix: small glossary
- fencepost: a metadata marker written at rollout start that contains checksums and pointers used for deterministic rollback.
- compat_checksum: short hash of runtime binary + proto descriptors used to detect silent API drift.
- mirror-only: traffic mirroring mode where responses are not used for decisioning, only telemetry collection.

Notes: This scaffold is intentionally conservative. For minor, safe bugfixes we can shorten cadence, but major control-plane/runtime bumps should follow the full scaffold above. Please leave review notes inline and add customer-specific exceptions to the rollout ticket rather than this template.
